## F134: background payload boundaries

Completion tails, titles in all completion states, inline event text **and data**, final-event suffixes and cold-owner subject titles use the shared debug-escaped quoted renderer. Inline and final turns explicitly describe the values as source-written; tails are labelled as the job's output (`crates/daemon/src/background.rs:1131-1143,1397-1409,1632-1653,1717-1805`).

Tail selection occurs on complete characters, keeps the last 1,200 and reports truncation before applying the quoted renderer. Titles use the 120-character rendering cap; inline data retains its 400-character/file fallback and the combined inline body its 4,000-character fallback. Escaping completes each scalar and generates its own closing quote, so the cut cannot expose an unfinished quote or raw newline/control sequence.

The separate completion JSON and batch-file serialization are unchanged. File-backed payloads and subsequently read job/source data remain untrusted; they are not converted into daemon instructions or permission merely by being returned by a daemon.

## F133: scope and folder checks

The digest fences the actual scope at render time, so old stored or derived paths are covered without trusting new admission (`crates/core/src/pa_digest.rs:157-168`).

Shared admission rejects control characters and U+2028/U+2029 through `printable_path`, with the constant `UnprintableFolder` reason and no rejected-path echo (`crates/core/src/admission.rs:145-171`). Registration uses that admission decision before committing the descriptor (`crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:950-960`); spawn uses the same predicate beside its absolute-path check. The refusal test verifies an existing worker's folder stays unchanged, no probe seat is minted and no event is published.

Printability is not canonicalization, ownership or a filesystem permission check. This patch protects the digest headline, not a universal promise that every operator-configured log/batch/recovery path elsewhere is model-framed.

## Retained interpretation limits

`fenced()` preserves a single-line quoted **structural** boundary. It is neither shell quoting nor semantic prompt-injection prevention. Instructions can still be read inside a source-labelled quotation; intentional request bodies, workflow prose and file-backed content require normal untrusted-input handling. No caller/owner/delivery authority is widened by these format changes.

The pre-reviewed #185 renderer qualifications remain. A future rebase onto another #185 head is not covered by this pinned verdict and needs the promised base-only delta.
